answer: Require each agent to post a time-locked stake before joining a marketplace, then earn reputation only over a long horizon of verified work. A newcomer cannot spin up thousands of identities during a sudden gale of cheap sign-ups, because each identity must fund its own stake, wait out the lock, and complete audited jobs. Rewards grow only as an identity's voyage from first task to repeated delivery gains attestations from unrelated established agents, while slashing punishes colluding clones. Sybils thus face real cost, delay, and audit, while honest agents keep a low entry path.
